We have reference losses for similar settings:

- Ref 1: 5 layers, width 128, no residual, mixed activations, some layer norm → 0.08611 (best)
- Ref 2: 4 layers, width 16, no residual, some layer norm → 0.6507
- Ref 3: 1 layer, width 16, layer norm, silu → 0.7837
- Ref 4: 2 layers, width 128, layer norm on first layer only, leaky_relu + silu → 0.3987
- Ref 5: 1 layer, width 256, no layer norm, leaky_relu → 0.7286

Key patterns:
- Wider and deeper helps a lot (Ref 1 vs Ref 2/3/5).
- 2 layers with width 128 (Ref 4) gives 0.3987, much worse than 5 layers width 128 (Ref 1).
- Layer norm on all layers might help or hurt; Ref 1 has mixed norms and is best.

Option A: 2 layers, width 128, layer norm on both layers, relu + gelu.  
This is similar to Ref 4 but with both layers normed and different activations. Ref 4 got 0.3987, so A likely around that range, maybe slightly better or worse but not near 0.086.

Option B: 5 layers, width 128, residual connections, no layer norm, silu/gelu mix.  
This is close to Ref 1 (5 layers, width 128) but with residual connections and no layer norm. Ref 1 had 0.08611. Residual connections often help or at least don't hurt much, so B could be similar or better than Ref 1.

Thus B is likely lower loss.

Answer: B
